verses.text: "How terrible for the shepherds who are destroying and scattering the sheep of my pasture!" says the LORD.

So this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says to the shepherds who take care of my people: "You have scattered my flock and driven them away. You have not taken care of them. So I will punish you for the evil you have done," says the LORD.
"I myself will gather the survivors of my flock from all the countries where I have driven them. I will bring them back to their pasture, and they will have many children and grow in number.
I will place shepherds over them who will take care of them. They will no longer be afraid or terrified, and none of them will be missing," says the LORD.
"Look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch. He will rule as king and act wisely. He will do what is fair and right in the land.
In his days Judah will be saved, and Israel will live in safety. This is the name he will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness.
So look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when people will no longer say, 'As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the people of Israel up out of Egypt.'

Instead they will say, 'As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the descendants of Israel up out of the land of the north and out of all the countries where he had driven them.' Then they will live in their own land."
About the prophets: My heart is broken inside me. All my bones tremble. I am like a drunk man, like someone overcome by wine, because of the LORD and his holy words.

"The land is full of people who are unfaithful in marriage. Because of the curse, the land mourns, and the pastures in the wilderness are dried up. The prophets follow an evil path and use their power in the wrong way.
Both prophets and priests are godless. Even in my temple I find their wickedness," says the LORD.
"So their path will become slippery, and they will be driven into darkness and fall there. For I will bring disaster on them in the year they are punished," says the LORD.
"Among the prophets of Samaria I saw something disgusting. They prophesied by Baal and led my people Israel astray.

And among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen something horrible. They commit adultery and live a lie. They encourage those who do evil, so that no one turns away from their wickedness. To me they are all like Sodom, and the people of Jerusalem are like Gomorrah."

So this is what the LORD of Armies says about the prophets: "Look, I will make them eat bitter food and drink poisoned water, because from the prophets of Jerusalem godlessness has spread throughout the land."
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "Do not listen to what the prophets are telling you. They fill you with false hopes. They speak visions from their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD.
They keep saying to those who hate me, 'The LORD says you will have peace.' And to all who follow their stubborn hearts they say, 'No harm will come to you.'
But which of them has stood in the council of the LORD to see and hear his word? Who has listened and heard his message?
Look, the storm of the LORD will burst out in fury, a whirlwind swirling down on the heads of the wicked.
The anger of the LORD will not turn back until he has fully carried out the plans of his heart. In the days to come you will understand this clearly.
I did not send these prophets, yet they have run with their message. I did not speak to them, yet they have prophesied.
But if they had stood in my council, they would have announced my words to my people. They would have turned them from their evil ways and their evil actions.
Am I only a God who is nearby," says the LORD, "and not a God who is far away?
Can anyone hide in secret places so that I cannot see them?" says the LORD. "Do I not fill heaven and earth?" says the LORD.
"I have heard what the prophets say who prophesy lies in my name. They say, 'I had a dream! I had a dream!'
How long will this go on in the hearts of these lying prophets, who prophesy the deceitful ideas of their own minds?
They think the dreams they tell one another will make my people forget my name, just as their ancestors forgot my name by worshiping Baal.
Let the prophet who has a dream tell his dream, but let the one who has my word speak my word faithfully. What does straw have to do with grain?" says the LORD.
"Is not my word like fire," says the LORD, "and like a hammer that breaks a rock into pieces?
So look, I am against the prophets," says the LORD, "who steal my words from one another.
Look, I am against the prophets," says the LORD, "who use their own tongues and then say, 'The LORD says.'

Look, I am against those who prophesy false dreams," says the LORD. "They tell them and lead my people astray with their reckless lies. I did not send them or appoint them. They do not help these people at all," says the LORD.
"When these people, or a prophet, or a priest asks you, 'What is the burden, the message from the LORD?' say to them, 'What burden? I will throw you away, says the LORD.'
If a prophet or a priest or anyone else says, 'This is the burden from the LORD,' I will punish that person and their household.
This is what each of you should keep saying to your friends and relatives: 'What answer has the LORD given?' or 'What has the LORD spoken?'
But you must no longer mention 'the burden from the LORD,' for each person's own words become their burden. You twist the words of the living God, the LORD of Armies, our God.
This is what you should say to a prophet: 'What answer has the LORD given you?' or 'What has the LORD spoken?'

But if you say, 'This is the burden from the LORD,' then this is what the LORD says: 'You used the words, "This is the burden from the LORD," even though I told you not to say, "This is the burden from the LORD."
So I will surely forget you and throw you out of my presence, along with the city I gave to you and your ancestors.
I will bring on you everlasting disgrace, everlasting shame that will never be forgotten.'"
